title: Living and non-living things are bound alike by physical and mathematical law

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Living and non-living things are bound alike by physical and mathematical law

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Living and non-living things alike are governed by the same physical and mathematical laws.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The living and the dead, things animate and inanimate, we dwellers in the world and this world wherein we dwell,—πάντα γα μὰν τὰ γιγνωσκόμενα,—are bound alike by physical and mathematical law.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), the Epilogue; topic “Mathematical law and beauty”. Scope: all living and non-living matter

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-epilogue-03: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.18

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Many narrower biophysical predictions are empirically testable, but observations are necessarily described mathematically and cannot exhaust all living and non-living matter. The statement has no discriminating finite dataset consequence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Specific physical laws can be tested in living and non-living systems, but the unrestricted assertion that all are governed by physical and mathematical law supplies no finite distinctive test.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No rival or boundary condition is specified.

The claim is universal and metaphysical.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.1
data adequacy: 0.08

operationalizability: 0.18
data existence: 0.3

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a general metaphysical commitment of the book. Particular physical relations elsewhere in the text can be tested with data. The epilogue sentence itself names no variable and no outcome that would count as confirmation or refutation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim says living and non-living things are governed by the same physical and mathematical laws. Without a specified law and a specified violation, no dataset distinguishes this from a rival that reserves some biological phenomena for other principles.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Any particular biophysical success confirms only that case, and the sentence names no case.
